rows.why: A: unrepealed morality statute enforced against foreigners (deportations), brutal custody, no recourse, hostile state — outing risks detention in a system reporting torture. B: enforced hostile border/document regime and facility bans, but rule of law, hate-crime and employment protections, courts blocking orders.

A imposes universal traveller exposure: passport/visa sex-marker regime, fraud-based bans, facility exclusion, custody abuse and official threat-framing. B criminalises nothing trans-specific, but documented police identity-check harassment and arbitrary arrests with no recourse remain unresolved.

A: tier-1 universal exposures — facility bans, birth-sex custody, visa/document flagging — but functioning courts and no anti-trans statute. B: criminalisation, collapsed rule of law, documented arrests, custodial death, presidential incitement; thin trans data resolves low.

A: state-imposed universal exposure — visa/document fraud flagging, facility bans with arrests, custody harm, official threat-framing. B: no trans-specific offence, no documented targeting or facility bans, only thin recourse and conservative attitudes.
